timeline.title: A Short History of Stargazing
items: Galileo looks up
Galileo turned an early telescope to the sky and soon saw mountains on the Moon and moons around Jupiter.
A new planet
William Herschel spotted Uranus from his garden, the first planet found with a telescope.
Footprints on the Moon
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon while about 600 million people watched.
Hubble opens its eyes
The Hubble Space Telescope launched and began sending back pictures of galaxies far, far away.
today: The brightest discovery of all. {age} trips around the Sun, and still dazzling.

letters.hand: They all looked up and wondered. We look at you and feel the same, {who}.

facts.title: The Astonishing Science of You
items: star
Made of star stuff
The calcium in your bones and the iron in your blood were made inside stars long ago.
globe
Your space mileage
Every birthday, you have ridden the Earth nearly a billion kilometres around the Sun.
sun
Eight minute sunshine
Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach you. You always see the Sun as it was moments ago.
eye
A time machine
Look at a star and you see light that left it years, even centuries, before you were born.
spark
The sky has moved
Earth slowly wobbles, so the stars behind the Sun on your birthday have shifted since ancient times.
moon
The thirteenth sign
The Sun also passes through Ophiuchus, a constellation the old zodiac left out.
facts.hand: The horoscope is just for fun. The star stuff is completely true, {who}.

note.title: What we believe about stars
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
Horoscopes are a bit of fun. But here is something true: you are made of atoms forged in stars billions of years ago, and they came together, against all the odds, as you.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not a card anyone could buy, but pages full of you: your face, your sparkle, the little things that make you, you.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you light up their whole sky.
